quoted_statement: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.

quoted_statement: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

quoted_statement: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.

quoted_statement: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.

quoted_statement: The exact canonical equivalence criterion for finite posets. For a finite poset $P$ define the colimit-preserving transform \[ (V_PF)(s)= \lim_{t\in P^{\mathrm{op}}} \bigl(\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_P(t,s)\otimes F(t)\bigr), \qquad V_P:\mathbb D(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb D(P^{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{G.9a} \] There is always a canonical formula \[ p_*^P\simeq p_!^{P^{\mathrm{op}}}V_P. \tag{G.9b} \] For spectra the transform (G.9a) is an equivalence if and only if each strict upper interval $P_{>p}$ is Gorenstein* over $\mathbb Z$. quoted_statement: Universal Cat-colimit shapes without a weakly terminal object. For a connected countable category $I$ without a weakly terminal object, and hence also in general, the implication from the universal ordinary-Cat-colimit comparison to filteredness remains unresolved here. F.4 gives a necessary totality condition and the full weakly-terminal case. The unbounded injective-ordinal examples do not refute this implication: the diagram $[n]\mapsto B\mathbb N^{n+1}$ has categorical colimit $B\mathbb N\simeq S^1$, whereas its Grothendieck construction has integral homology $\mathbb Z$ in every degree. On all of $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ its degree-$k$ fibre homology, for $k\geq1$, is the projective representable $\mathbb Z[\Delta_{\rm inj}([k-1],-)]$; the homotopy-colimit spectral sequence collapses. On an arbitrary unbounded full subcategory $A_S$, the restricted diagram need not be representable. Instead its higher derived colimits vanish by exactness in F.3, and its colimit is $\mathbb Z$: any two marked $k$-element ordered subsets admit embeddings into a common larger ordinal identifying their marks, then into an object of $A_S$. The categorical colimit is still $B\mathbb N$, since the same embeddings identify all coordinate generators and introduce precisely their commutative-monoid relation. Thus all these shapes fail the premise. This prevents importing the nonfiltered total example as an answer to the different Cat-colimit question.

Let $\mathcal C$ be either $\operatorname{Sp}_{\mathcal U}$ or $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with its indicated presentable infinity-category enhancement. We number the stages by \[ W_{\mathcal C}^{(0)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \mathcal C_1=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{I.9.1} \] Here $\mathcal S_W$ is the accessible reflective localization of spaces at exactly the class $W$, and $\mathbb D_{\mathcal E}(A)=\operatorname{Ho}\operatorname{Fun}(NA^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)$. The localizations in (I.9.1) exist and preserve finite products. Their constant-coefficient classes satisfy $W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}$. For every map $u:X\to Y$ of small spaces, \[ u\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xu\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}. \tag{I.9.2} \] The loop condition is tested at one basepoint in every component of $X$. Consequently \[ W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(1)} =W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(2)}=W_\infty, \tag{I.9.3} \] and \[ u\in W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_i(u)\text{ is an integral isomorphism for }i=1,2,\\ H_*(u\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p)\text{ is an isomorphism}. \end{cases} \tag{I.9.4} \] For a pointed connected component, $X\langle2\rangle$ means the homotopy fibre at its chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\leq2}X$. The map $u\langle2\rangle:X\langle2\rangle\to Y\langle2\rangle$ is induced by $u$ and the basepoints. The last two conditions of (I.9.4) are tested on every corresponding pointed component. quoted_statement: Let $S$ be an ordinary small category, regarded as a locally discrete strict $2$-category. On $2\operatorname{Cat}/S$ define the presheaf fine class by requiring $s\backslash u$ to be a Street weak equivalence for every $s\in S$. Its infinity-localization is equivalent to $\operatorname{Fun}(NS^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. The dual over-slice class gives $\operatorname{Fun}(NS,\mathcal S)$. These equivalences are compatible with the Street-nerve comparisons to the contravariant and covariant simplicial theories over $NS$.

quoted_statement: The universally pullback-preserving classes in Part J(2), the complete boundary-piece tests, and the proposed lax-comma Der~4 base-change theorem in J(3) are not established here. The absolute model structure and Theorem A do not imply those claims. The verified statements available from the sources are Theorem A for the specified slices \citep[Theorem 5.2]{GHIJAraMaltsiniotis2018} and invariance under every cell duality \citep[Theorem 6.6]{GHIJAraMaltsiniotis2022}. Reversing only $2$-cells exchanges lax and oplax coherence; reversing all positive-dimensional cells exchanges the matched under/over fine theories. A full four-variance base-change table requires the still-missing recognition and lax-comma compatibility.
